author: 5kO0
content:
Surfaced by #22's wild-corpus rustc-compile test. Three concrete instances in a 420-lexicon slice of the wild corpus (app+chat+com+tools, scraped 2026-05-08):

  com.deckbelcher.richtext + com.deckbelcher.richtext.facet
    → emits com/deckbelcher/richtext.rs AND com/deckbelcher/richtext/mod.rs (collision)
  com.alephcubed.starmark.review + com.alephcubed.starmark.review.{book,game,movie,tvshow}
    → emits review.rs AND review/mod.rs
  app.beaconbits.beacon + app.beaconbits.beacon.like
    → emits beacon.rs AND beacon/mod.rs

rustc says: 'file for module \`X\` found at both \"<path>.rs\" and \"<path>/mod.rs\"' (E0761).

Root cause (predicted, not yet read in source): when an NSID is BOTH a leaf (e.g. com.deckbelcher.richtext) and a namespace prefix for child NSIDs (com.deckbelcher.richtext.facet), the codegen treats them independently — writes the leaf as <name>.rs AND creates a <name>/ subdir for children with mod.rs. In Rust 2018+, only one of these is legal per module path.

Fix shape: when NSID X is both a leaf and a parent, inline the leaf's content INTO X/mod.rs (and don't write X.rs). Or use the inverse: keep X.rs as the leaf and write children under X/<child>.rs without a mod.rs — but that's harder because Rust looks up child modules via the parent's mod-path declaration.

Most likely landing in proto-blue-codegen/src/main.rs::write_output and/or generator.rs's mod-tree-emitting code. Search for where mod.rs is synthesised vs where leaf .rs is written; the fork-detection logic there is the bug.

This is exactly the audit's predicted "weird shit people do with lexicons" — three independent third-party publishers happened to nest a namespace under a leaf. The bundled bsky/atproto/chat/tools corpus doesn't contain this pattern, which is why the bundled 322-doc test compiles cleanly while the wild slice surfaces it.
